titleEn: Hrīṃ is the Devī — the heart-seed at the centre of Navārṇa.
meaningHi: बीज का शब्दकोश में कोई अर्थ नहीं होता। तंत्र ह्रीं को देवी का अपना बीज मानते हैं — भुवनेश्वरी का। नवार्ण मंत्र के बीच में यही आता है: ऐं ह्रीं क्लीं।
meaningEn: A bīja has no dictionary meaning. The Tantras read hrīṃ as the māyā-seed — the Devī's own sound, Bhuvaneśvarī — and it stands in the middle of the Navārṇa mantra you may already know: aiṃ hrīṃ klīṃ.

words.glossEn: the closing hum — bindu and nāda
words.glossHi: अंत की गूँज — बिन्दु और नाद

source.text: Varada Tantra as quoted in Woodroffe, Garland of Letters (1922); Śāradā-tilaka Tantra (11th c.)
source.note: The syllable-by-syllable reading is the Tantras' kośa method — an attribution with authority inside those lineages, not etymology.

significance.textSays: The Tantras read it as ha = Śiva, ra = prakṛti, ī = māyā, closing in bindu and nāda — Śiva and Śakti fused in one sound.
significance.traditionSays: The māyā-bīja; Bhuvaneśvarī's seed; second of the three Navārṇa seeds. In Śākta practice it is received from a guru.
significance.weDoNotClaim: Any effect from saying it. A bīja has no dictionary meaning; we show tradition's reading and name the text.

practice.dikshaNote: Many lineages receive this from a guru; here you learn its meaning.
